title: Global uniform regularity and vanishing vertical viscosity limit for the compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the half-space
summary: In geophysical flows such as large-scale ocean dynamics, the vertical viscosity is often much smaller than the horizontal viscosity. This anisotropy makes it natural to ask whether solutions of the full anisotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations converge, as the vertical viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon \to 0$, to solutions of a horizontally dissipative limit system, and whether this limit can be justified globally in time.
